entry.content:
Logback vulnerable to Object Injection through HardenedObjectInputStream modules

Aliases: CVE-2026-10532

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N/E:P/RE:M/U:Green

Deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in QOS.CH Sarl logback logback-core (HardenedObjectInputStream (logback-core) modules) allows Object Injection, albeit heavily restricted. More precisely, an attacker able to influence serialized data sent to SimpleSocketServer or SimpleSSLSocketServer can instantiate Proxy objects. Although deserialization is heavily restricted by HardenedObjectInputStream and no practical way to achieve remote code execution or significant privilege escalation has been identified, this issue constitutes a bypass of the intended security restrictions. This issue affects logback: through 1.5.33 inclusive.

Druid ingestion system Authenticated users can read data from other sources than intended

Aliases: CVE-2021-26920, CVE-2023-26920, GHSA-x3cc-x39p-42qx

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.apache.druid:druid-core — fixed in 0.21.0

In the Druid ingestion system, the InputSource is used for reading data from a certain data source. However, the HTTP InputSource allows authenticated users to read data from other sources than intended, such as the local file system, with the privileges of the Druid server process. This is not an elevation of privilege when users access Druid directly, since Druid also provides the Local InputSource, which allows the same level of access. But it is problematic when users interact with Druid indirectly through an application that allows users to specify the HTTP InputSource, but not the Local InputSource. In this case, users could bypass the application-level restriction by passing a file URL to the HTTP InputSource.

entry.content:
Vulnerability in RPKI manifest validation

Aliases: CVE-2020-16164

Affected:

  • net.ripe.rpki:rpki-validator-3 — fixed in 3.2-2020.10.28.23.06

A vulnerability in RPKI manifest validation exists when objects on the manifest are hidden, or expired objects are replayed. An attacker successfully exploiting this vulnerability could prevent new ROAs from being received or selectively hide ROAs, causing routes to become INVALID. To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would need to perform a man in the middle attack on the TLS connection between the validator and an RRDP repository or perform a man in the middle attack against a rsync-only repository. The update addresses the vulnerability by implementing validation methods from [RFC 6486bis](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-sidrops-6486bis/00/) and enabling strict validation by default.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-36hp-jr8h-556f: Authentication Bypass
entry.content:
Authentication Bypass

Aliases: CVE-2021-29441, CVE-2021-29442, GHSA-xv5h-v7jh-p2qh

Affected:

  • com.alibaba.nacos:nacos-common — fixed in 1.4.1

When configured to use authentication (`-Dnacos.core.auth.enabled=true`) Nacos uses the `AuthFilter` servlet filter to enforce authentication. ### Impact `StaticFile.fromUrl` can leak the presence of a directory on a server when the `URL` scheme is not `file://`, and the URL points to a fetchable resource under its scheme and authority.
